problem: Iteration-1 FIND-006 (blocker) objected that PROP-7's human-funded V4 leg ('bank receipt') had no defined zero-human mechanism and would likely require a human-assisted bank login/2FA, contradicting REQ-2. The revision renames the check from 'bank receipt' to 'a platform-confirmed sale event (note / Stripe / Substack API or dashboard showing the paid sale)' and explicitly moves bank withdrawal out of scope as a one-time human install step. This narrows the KYC/withdrawal problem but does NOT resolve the underlying zero-human-verification problem it was raised against -- it relocates it: the spec still asserts, as a REQUIRED (T3) gate, that the skill will autonomously read a note.com/Substack dashboard or an unnamed 'API' to confirm a sale event, with zero specification of (a) which of these platforms actually expose a programmatic sale-event API (unverified factual claim -- note.com in particular is not known to expose a public sales API), (b) whether dashboard access requires a login session that could expire and trigger 2FA/OTP mid-loop, or (c) how that access loops back to REQ-13's 'stored creds / Gmail-OTP auto-read / CapSolver+camofox' fallback in a way that is actually tested. Sprint 2 (verification-architecture.md:57) names 'note ¥500 reaches V4 (PROP-7,8, T3 live)' as THE money finish-line for the whole feature, so this hand-wave sits directly on the critical path of the sprint the entire spec exists to prove.
fix: Before marking PROP-7's human-funded leg required:true, name the CONCRETE mechanism for Sprint 2's target rail (note): e.g. 'note.com dashboard is read via the install's persisted CloakBrowser session (REQ-15 creds); if a login/2FA challenge appears, REQ-13's Gmail-OTP auto-read pattern (already proven for Instagram, REQ-11) is invoked; PROP-7's T3 test asserts the sale-event read completes with zero Dais-relayed input.' If no such mechanism can be named today, explicitly descope the human-funded leg of PROP-7 from Sprint 2's required gates (mark it an open risk) rather than asserting an unverified 'API/dashboard' check as done.
